TECHD.why: About 3x the ₹193 issue price (52-week range ₹360-844; reported up 51% over a year). The sources give no direct cause; drivers cited from filings: FY26 profit up 67% to ₹14.0 crore and income up 76% to ₹53.3 crore, an order book of ₹70 crore (up 63% from ₹43 crore at March 2026) after the largest single order to date (₹13.08 crore including GST, October 2026). Investor Vijay Kedia held over 5% at March 2026.
TECHD.outlook: Management targets 40-50% revenue growth, about 100% from FY27 on global expansion (third-party summary), and $80-100 million revenue by 2030. These are company targets, not analyst forecasts. P/E about 30-32 and price-to-book near 6, so expectations are high.

PRARUH.why: About 2.3x the ₹63 issue price after listing flat at ₹63.20 on weak subscription. It rose about 178% from about ₹52 in June to ₹144.60 (upper circuit) on 16 September 2026, from a ₹45 low in March. No explanation was found; a partnership with Quantum Networks (15 September) and a ₹33.5 crore RailTel order (May) are the nearest news items. Promoters hold about 73%, leaving a small free float.
PRARUH.outlook: No analyst targets or guidance found, and the FY26 results (29 May 2026) were not summarised in the sources. The rally looks momentum-driven; verify the Quantum Networks details and FY26 results on the exchange.

INFINITY.why: About 3.5x the ₹155 issue price after listing at ₹294.50 (+90%). It rose sharply in 2026 (about ₹384 on 14 August to about ₹543 on 21 September; 55% in six months). No explanation was found. FY26 revenue rose to ₹24.5 crore from ₹13.5 crore and profit to ₹7.0 crore from ₹4.4 crore, with ROE 47% and almost no debt, but receivables are 157 days. It sells cloud ERP and a campus-management system used in 26 universities.
INFINITY.outlook: No analyst target or guidance found. P/E 29-43 and price-to-book 4-5. A Q1 FY27 earnings call was held on 13 August 2026; its contents were not retrievable.

WORKMATES.why: About 2x the ₹204 issue price (listed at ₹387.60, +90%), but no sustained 2026 rally: 52-week range ₹264-514 and roughly -14% in six months. It jumped 10% to ₹332 after FY26 results: revenue rose 34% to ₹143.8 crore and profit 16% to ₹15.9 crore, with recurring revenue at 82.5% of sales. Revenue slipped 9% from H1 (₹75 crore) to H2 (₹68 crore).
WORKMATES.outlook: Management targets ₹210 crore FY27 revenue (45%+ growth) and PAT of about ₹24-25 crore, with ₹160 crore of annual contracted revenue already secured, and AI as the main growth engine from FY28; one source gives a more conservative ₹200 crore and ₹550 crore by FY30. These are management targets. P/E 23-34.

LOGICIEL.why: Down about 83% from the ₹193 issue price after a 24% discount debut (₹146.70) in December 2025, and down 53.5% year to date by July 2026 (52-week range ₹28-154). The sources cite general negative sentiment, thin trading and bearish technicals, not a company event. FY25 profit was reported at ₹5.47 crore on revenue of ₹21.2 crore with ROE 33% and almost no debt.
LOGICIEL.outlook: No formal analyst rating or management outlook found. Simply Wall St scores future growth 0 of 6. In July 2026 the board approved making its US entity a wholly owned subsidiary. Market cap is only about ₹24 crore.

METHODHUB.why: Down about 62% from the ₹194 issue price: it hit ₹60.94 on 4 September 2026 (a 52-week low) and fell to the lower circuit at ₹74.65 on 24 September when it hit the lower circuit; down 57.6% year to date. No company announcement explained the falls. Reported FY26 revenue of about ₹333 crore (+147%) conflicts with other providers, so check filings. Reported P/E 4.0, P/B 0.8, ROE 42%.
METHODHUB.outlook: No analyst coverage or forecast found; a technical signal reads Strong Sell. Market cap was roughly ₹130-148 crore in September. The very low multiples alongside falling prices suggest the market is discounting something the sources do not name.

SHIPWAVES.why: Down about 73% from the ₹12 issue price and 69% over a year (52-week range ₹2.55-12). Promoter holding fell from 99.96% to 66.78% after the December 2025 IPO raised ₹56.35 crore with 4.7 crore new shares, which fits a post-listing sell-off. Operating cash flow was negative (-₹3.45 crore in FY25). It sells digital freight forwarding software.
SHIPWAVES.outlook: No analyst forecast or guidance found; ROE figures conflict (30% vs 2.4%). Price is below its 20- and 50-day averages.

MOBILISE.why: About 1.2x the ₹80 issue price. It listed at ₹64.10 (a 20% discount) despite a 100x subscribed IPO, then climbed to about ₹108-113 by August-September 2026 (52-week range ₹45-126). FY26 revenue rose to ₹18.8 crore from ₹16.2 crore and profit to ₹5.6 crore from ₹4.8 crore. Debtor days rose from 48 to 83. No cause for the rally was stated; promoters hold 70.7%.
MOBILISE.outlook: No analyst target or guidance found. MarketScreener shows a model-estimated 2026 P/E of 6.8x. The small free float means large price swings.

ACETECH.why: Slightly above the ₹112 issue price after a flat debut (IPO subscribed only 1.1x), reaching ₹126 by June 2026. Reported annual revenue is about ₹82.8 crore (+17.6%) with profit about ₹10.3 crore. IPO money goes to marketing, working capital and acquisitions. Promoters hold 64.4%; trading is thin.
ACETECH.outlook: No analyst forecast or 2026 guidance found. P/E is about 22. The online retail and marketplace model relies on digital marketing and working capital growth.
